title: Training module — a way to learn something, never a way to prove it
description:
Governs content/competence/modules/<domain>/<id>.yaml. A module helps a person LEARN. It is one route among many and never a gate: self-study, mentoring, a commercial course and prior practice are equally legitimate ways to arrive at the same assessment, and the competence definition stays independent of any learning provider.

Completing a module produces a TRAINING RECORD, not a credential. Training completed is not competence demonstrated — that equation is the failure this whole project exists to reject, and it would be perverse to reintroduce it in the training layer. See training-record.schema.json, where `attestsCompetence` is const false.

WHAT A MODULE IS NOT FOR. It is not a workaround for equipment access. A person can read everything ever written about a CMM and still be unable to run one; that is a fact about the competence, not a defect to engineer around. Elements whose `demonstration` is `equipment` are evidenced by witnessed work on real apparatus and that requirement stands. A module's job is to make the eventual bench time count, not to replace it.

The test is `demonstration`, NOT `kind`. `skill` means the evidence is observable performance rather than explanation; it does not mean the performance happens at a bench, and constructing an uncertainty budget is a skill and is desk work. Telling a learner they are blocked on equipment they never needed invents a barrier, which the validator rejects exactly as it rejects hiding a real one. See `requiresPhysicalDemonstration` below.

SCOPE, DELIBERATELY LIMITED. Procedural simulation: interactive diagrams, parametric widgets, guided worked examples, walkthroughs. NOT virtual instrumentation — a 3D instrument you handle with a mouse teaches the handling of a mouse, becomes a toy rather than a competency module, and does not fit a serverless USB-distributable build anyway.

format.description:
Everything here must run bundled, offline and deterministically: the default build makes no external calls, the Personal edition is serverless and USB-distributable, and no AI ships. That rules out streamed video, hosted simulators and adaptive tutors, and it favours small parametric SVG or canvas work over heavy assets.

`virtual-instrumentation` is deliberately absent from this list.

knowledgeRefs.description: The BOK sections this module teaches. REQUIRED: a module is a route through the corpus, not a parallel corpus. Teaching material that exists only inside a module is knowledge the BOK has lost, and a person who did not take the module cannot reach it.

preparesFor.description: The assessable units this module helps someone approach. PREPARES FOR, not qualifies for, and not a prerequisite — nothing here may be required before an assessment. Someone who learned it on the bench twenty years ago sits the same assessment without ever opening this.

route.description:
Which evidence route this module prepares, for a target element that declares MORE THAN ONE in `demonstration`. Required there, and forbidden anywhere else: where the element declares a single route it has already answered the question, and restating it here creates a second copy of one fact that can drift out of agreement with the element after an edit.

THE MULTI-ROUTE CASE IS THE ONE SILENCE GETS WRONG. Both routes are admissible for such an element, so neither listing the target in `requiresPhysicalDemonstration` nor omitting it is inherently an error — and a module that simply said nothing would leave a learner bound for the instrument route with no warning that bench access is coming, while validating perfectly cleanly. Stating the route is what makes `requiresPhysicalDemonstration` checkable rather than decided by omission.

requiresPhysicalDemonstration.description:
Elements in `preparesFor` that this module prepares by the EQUIPMENT route — physical apparatus the learner may not have access to. See `demonstration` on the element, which declares the routes by which the competence can be evidenced at all.

WHICH TARGETS BELONG HERE IS DERIVED, NOT DECLARED, and the validator checks it in both directions. Where the element declares `[equipment]` alone it must appear here: a module claiming to complete such an element by simulation is asserting that a simulation substitutes for the bench, and it does not — the failure would otherwise be invisible, because the module would look complete and the learner would believe they had finished something they have never done. Where the element declares `[desk]` alone it must NOT appear here: inventing a barrier is as wrong as hiding one, and listing it tells a learner they are waiting for access they never needed. Where the element declares BOTH routes, this list must agree with the `route` stated on the `preparesFor` entry.

NOT every skill element. `skill` means the evidence is observable performance rather than explanation; it does not mean the performance happens at a bench. Constructing an uncertainty budget is a skill and is desk work.

Completing the module puts the elements listed here into `pending-demonstration` on the training record: the knowledge is done, the demonstration is not. That is an accurate statement of position rather than an encouraging one, which is what makes it useful — a mentor or a laboratory reading it knows exactly what is being asked for.

cannotConvey.description:
REQUIRED, and the field most likely to get a module rejected. State plainly what this format cannot teach.

Some competences are perceptual and no simulation reaches them. Dimensional work is the type case: measuring force, the feel of a correctly wrung gauge block stack, the point at which a thimble slips, the moment an anvil is not square to the work. A module that pretends otherwise produces a candidate who believes they can do something they have never done, which is worse than no training at all.

This is the training-layer counterpart of `lookupResistance` on an archetype: a required, unfakeable sentence that forces the author to confront the limit of what they have built.

assets.description: Bundled files the module needs. Paths inside the repository — anything fetched at runtime fails the air-gap check.

alternativeRoutes.description: Other legitimate ways to learn this — a textbook, a standard, a mentor, a commercial course, prior practice. Named generically and never as an endorsement: the corpus is vendor-neutral and content steering readers toward a particular provider is rejected. Recorded so the module reads as one option rather than the path.
